name: Calibration & QA
author: @opensmell
tagline: Guided sensor calibration and quality assurance.
summary: Walks through zero/span calibration per channel, validates sensor health, and exports a clean calibration report. Advisory only — not a certified calibration service.
scope: Supports one-time and repeat calibration of gas sensors on a known rig. Use before deploying anomaly detection or comparative measurements.
limits: Not a certified calibration service. Results depend on the quality of your reference gas and setup.
MOX sensors require stable warmup (~300 s) before calibration is meaningful.
NDIR/PID/electrochemical sensors need their own reference gas and flow path.
Export is a record of what you did; it does not prove accuracy.

widgets.headline: Calibration is only as good as your reference gas.
widgets.body: A calibration curve transfers trust from a known concentration to your sensor. If the reference gas is wrong, the calibration is wrong.
always: Use clean, zero-grade air for the zero step.
Use a known concentration gas for the span step.
Let sensors warm up fully before starting.
Record temperature and humidity — they affect calibration.
never: Do not use exhaled breath as a reference gas.
Do not calibrate against an uncalibrated sensor.
Do not present calibration output as certified or traceable.

widgets.title: Calibration log
widgets.description: Record the conditions that affect calibration: reference gas, concentration, flow rate, temperature, humidity.

logFields.label: Observation
logFields.placeholder: stable drift, sensor swap, new cartridge

rules.when: Baseline drift exceeds ±5% over 10 minutes in clean air
rules.then: Do not calibrate. Check for leaks, temperature swings, or sensor drift first.

rules.when: Channel is saturated (flat at rail) during span step
rules.then: Reduce concentration or check load resistor. Do not force a fit.
Wait. Calibration before warmup is meaningless.

rules.when: Post-calibration check reads within ±10% of reference
rules.then: Calibration accepted. Export report and proceed.

widgets.title: Use this with your rig
widgets.body: Connect a rig with at least one gas sensor channel. The vial reads per-channel warmup, baseline, and QC state from Osmograph and guides you through zero/span calibration. Compare recordings in Check on the same rig.

docs.title: How to calibrate
body: Connect your rig and let sensors warm up fully (MOX: ~300 s, NDIR: ~60 s).
Expose to clean zero-grade air and record the baseline (zero step).
Expose to a known concentration span gas and record the response (span step).
The vial fits the curve and exports a calibration report with R₀, slope, and residuals.
Repeat on a schedule — sensors drift. Recalibrate after sensor replacement or major temperature change.

docs.title: What it cannot do
body: It cannot certify traceability to NIST or any national standard.
It cannot calibrate without a reference gas of known concentration.
It cannot make an uncalibrated sensor trustworthy for safety decisions.
It cannot compensate for cross-sensitivity to humidity or other gases.
